text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright says U.S. troops presence in the Gulf region is the best way to deter any aggression against Kuwait.
- Kuwait's tobacco imports amount to 19 million dinars ($62.7 million) in 1995, official study says.

- Cabinet approves plan to deter infiltrations by Iraqis, cabinet minister tells parliamentarian. Scores of Iraqis have illegally crossed the closed Iraq-Kuwait border since the 1990-91 Gulf War to seek jobs, collect weapons left on the battlefield or to seek asylum in third countries.

- British royal yacht Britannia docks in Kuwait. Heir to Britan's throne Prince Charles, due in Kuwait on Friday for a two-day visit, will use Britannia as a base for official visits to the Gulf states of Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar.

- Kuwait did not receive any funds from a United Nations compensations fund, official says. Kuwait has filed claims worth over $116 billion for damages resulting from Iraq's occupation. A U.N. commission is in charge of managing Iraqi compensations.
